newsitem.title: FINLAND: Forestries and Nokia whip Helsinki to new record.
newsitem.headline: Forestries and Nokia whip Helsinki to new record.

text.p: Finnish shares closed at new highs on Tuesday after a strong recovery from Monday's losses, led by forestries powering ahead on hopes of higher prices and a restructuring arrangement between UPM-Kymmene and Metsa-Serla.
The HEX general index rose 1.85 percent to close at its new record of 2492.0 points and bourse engine Nokia rallied 9.30 markka to 268.00 markka.
Volume was a healthy 500 million markka.
Nokia's close was two markka above last Thursday's, before Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan's talk of "irrational exuberance" sent shockwaves around stockmarkets.
Brokers said renewed interest in forestries combined with Nokia strength in the U.S. could bring more records this year.

The forest industry index rose two percent in early dealings and added another 1.20 percent after Europe's largest paper maker UPM-Kymmene and Metsa-Serla said they were strengthening their joint pulp mill company Metsa-Botnia.

In the transactions, Metsa-Serla acquired some UPM assets to become number two in Europe in folding board and the deals gave UPM a 700 million markka gain, prompting some comments that UPM was the most attractive forestry stock.
UPM closed 3.70 markka higher at 97.70, up almost four percent, and trade was an active 66 million markka. Metsa-Serla advanced three percent to 35.00 markka.
Chemicals firm Kemira joined the rally after a newspaper report that it plans to raise its titanium dioxide price early next year. It closed up 2.60 markka or four percent at 58.90.
